blocks.cap: OpenAI at Advertising Week New York.

blocks.x: OpenAI is piloting brand suitability controls with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science, giving advertisers an independent read on how the ad safeguards in ChatGPT work, the company announced on Monday during Advertising Week New York.

The two verification firms will assess how OpenAI applies its brand safety standards in a controlled testing environment, without access to private user conversations. OpenAI says the goal is to give advertisers greater transparency into how those safeguards work while protecting conversation privacy.

Adweek notes that bringing in outside verification follows a path other platforms have taken to win over buyers wary of media sellers grading their own work, and that both firms already measure brand safety placements across TikTok, Meta and Reddit. The pilots here are narrower for now, and it is unclear whether either firm will measure placements in live campaigns.

OpenAI also launched Negative Phrases, which lets brands set placement exclusions specific to their own policies. The company confirmed it was testing the tool in August, after Adweek reported that advertisers were seeing ads misaligned with user conversations in ChatGPT.
Alongside this, OpenAI is testing a larger ad format led by images, which appears during image generation, and is expanding its roster of measurement partners.

blocks.cap: TikTok's announcement of its advertising updates.

blocks.x: At Advertising Week New York 2026, TikTok set out a package of agentic advertising and commerce updates spanning every stage of the customer journey.

On the selling side, TikTok says it is building new agentic commerce shopping experiences, starting with Buy Direct and Shopping Assistant, and building them with commerce and payment platforms including Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza and Stripe. Buy Direct is an in-app checkout that lets a shopper buy from a brand without leaving TikTok, in one click from the For You feed. Shopping Assistant is a conversational agent that handles product details, shipping, sizing, availability and purchase in a single conversation.
Agentic Leads is a separate agent for lead generation, running guided conversations in TikTok direct messages and in lead forms on advertisers' own websites.

On the buying side, TikTok is bringing its TikTok Ad Network to advertisers in the United States, extending campaigns across what it describes as a premium network of nearly 400,000 apps, and is opening Search Ads Campaign powered by Smart+ along with Smart+ Creative Selection, which gathers an advertiser's own assets, Symphony's generated creative and creator content into one approval workflow.

TikTok also says its business interface built on the open Model Context Protocol is now available as a connector across several platforms and registries, and that advertiser use of it for campaign activation has grown by more than 200%, citing its own internal data for July to September 2026.

blocks.cap: Digiday's coverage of Advertising Week in New York.

blocks.x: Omnicom Media has partnered with the advertising platform Rembrand on what it calls a first to market capability that lets brands identify, plan and activate placements inside premium streaming content.

The pair plan to use Rembrand's VISTA platform, which uses AI to scan publisher content and identify scenes that can be monetized. Omnicom Media's Content Collective, its branded content unit, then works the placements into the content. The aim is to scale placement inside content beyond isolated instances.

Omnicom Media picks the shows for a brand using its RealID audience product within Acxiom, matched against viewership data from streamers, then maps that against the opportunities in VISTA. A packaged goods client could be inserted into an episode of a cooking reality show after it has been produced and shot. Digiday notes the idea is not new, but doing it after production is.

Digiday reports the holding company's media network is still negotiating with several media companies that run streaming services, and could not name any of them. Megan Pagliuca, chief product officer for North America, said this is the first time the capability has been used by the buy side, having historically been a sell side technology, and called it still a nascent capability.

Omnicom Media's own research with Rembrand, rather than an independent study, found that placements inside content paired with traditional video ads drove a 5.5 times increase in message recall and a fourfold increase in both purchase intent and perception of the brand as premium.

blocks.cap: Gap's store in the Marina district of San Francisco in June 2026.

blocks.x: Gap Inc. is unveiling a suite of shopping tools built on AI across all of its brands, thirty years after it launched the first online store for its namesake Gap brand.

blocks.cap: Gap's first online store at its debut in 1996. Courtesy of Gap.

blocks.x: From Monday, Gap customers can discover items through two outside platforms. Alta Daily curates outfit suggestions from variables including a user's schedule, budget and the weather forecast, and can surface items from a shopper's existing wardrobe as well as brands' assortments. Daydream takes everyday language and returns fashion ideas, with access to all four Gap Inc. brands: Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta.
Old Navy and Banana Republic customers can describe what they are looking for in natural language to conversational shopping agents on those two brands' websites and apps.

Sven Gerjets, chief technology officer, says he is aware shoppers can be wary of or even disappointed by shopping experiences assisted by AI. Retail Dive cites a SmartCustomer survey last month finding 45% of purchases consumers regret making with AI help were apparel and footwear, and research from Synchrony and Oxford Economics finding consumers are more likely to shop with AI at retailers they already trust, but are wary of how their data is used.

Agentic media buying is all the rage, including for streaming TV. A new joint effort announced Tuesday will use custom agents to help brand marketers get more from their streaming TV investments, including upfront commitments. The initiative brings together NBCUniversal, its SSP FreeWheel, Dentsu-owned agency Carat and agentic analytics platform Newton.

Custom buying agents pair identity data from NBCU and FreeWheel with audience intelligence from Dentsu and Newton. The agent uses that audience data and ad performance data to recommend NBCU ad inventory based on an advertiser's desired outcome.

An unnamed luxury retailer working with Carat is the first marketer to use the solution, although the joint offering will eventually be available to all Dentsu clients. In the meantime, Carat is busy building custom agents for specific advertiser KPIs, everything from search lift to incremental reach.

The promise is that agents could bring outcomes-based buying closer to the mainstream in CTV. But if every buy is judged by immediate results, advertisers could end up sacrificing long-term brand building for short-term gains.
Google Merchant Center is rolling out the UCP integration hub in the United States. The UCP integration hub allows you to onboard to UCP program from your Merchant Center account.
The hub says "Start selling across AI surfaces by implementing Universal Commerce Protocol," with agentic actions on AI Mode, Gemini, and Search, starting with checkout directly on Google.

Google's help document, spotted by Hana Kobzova on PPC News, says: "The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is a new open standard for agentic commerce that enables agents and systems to work together across the commerce ecosystem. By integrating with UCP, you can implement a checkout button on eligible product listings in AI Mode in Google Search and on Gemini."

The Merchant Center integration is gradually rolling out in the U.S. right now, and will roll out to merchants in Australia and Canada next year. "This will allow you to onboard to the program from your Merchant Center account and enable capabilities like cart transfer to a merchant site and enhanced checkout flow testing," Google added.

blocks.x: Through its partnership with Accenture Song, Radisson Hotel Group is using OpenAI technology to reach guests earlier in the travel planning journey. The Radisson Hotels ChatGPT plugin helps travelers compare hotels and explore travel options, and early results show booking conversion approximately 1.5 times that of Radisson's organic search.

With the help of agentic development, the team built and launched the plugin in just six weeks. It lets users see Radisson Hotel suggestions on a map, compare pricing, and view hotel amenities in detail directly in ChatGPT, then continue to the Radisson site to complete their booking.
A recent ChatGPT update means users no longer have to type @RadissonHotels; if the plugin is installed, ChatGPT automatically shows it whenever relevant.

Radisson is also among the hospitality pioneers running sponsored advertising in ChatGPT. More than half of the campaign's recorded checkout and booking events were attributed through view-through measurement. The MCP server and APIs Accenture developed for the plugin also power the ads experience.

blocks.cap: Four hollow suits in twelve: up to a third of clicks on some ChatGPT ads were invalid

blocks.x: TrafficGuard, the ad verification platform owned by Adveritas Ltd, said an analysis of 40,021 clicks on OpenAI's ChatGPT ads found invalid rates between 0.1% and 34% depending on the advertiser, with four hosting and proxy networks behind 47% of the flagged clicks.

The clicks landed on 78 websites run by 47 enterprise advertisers between August 24 and September 14, 2026. On the worst-hit account, according to chief executive Mathew Ratty, "nearly 90% of flagged clicks came from server infrastructure with no human user behind it."

The four networks sent 899 clicks in three weeks, reached 25 of the 47 advertisers and produced 742 of the 1,592 invalid clicks. 1,336 ChatGPT clicks (3.34%) came from hosting, residential-proxy or malicious IP space, against 0.92% on the same advertisers' Google Ads.

TrafficGuard's figures count clicks that reached advertisers' websites, not clicks billed by OpenAI, and the company sells click verification, so the findings come from a party with a commercial interest.

blocks.cap: ChatGPT screens showing the new visual ad format alongside a generated image.

blocks.x: OpenAI is introducing a new visual ad format in ChatGPT, expanding its measurement tools and partnerships, and developing new ways to understand brand suitability. The company says ChatGPT reaches 1.2 billion people each week.

The format shows images of product inspiration, product usage, or the experiences a product makes possible. OpenAI will test it during image generation in ChatGPT, for users on the Free and Go plans. Ads will be clearly labeled and stay separate from the image being created, and the company says advertising does not influence the answers ChatGPT gives. Testing begins later this month in the United States with an initial group of advertisers.

On measurement, new integrations with Hightouch, Tealium and LiveRamp let advertisers send conversion data from their own systems into ChatGPT Ads, and OpenAI now supports a long list of attribution partners for its conversions interface, reporting and click attribution. Experiments comparing results across geographies, run with Haus, Measured and WorkMagic, are still at an early stage.

The performance figures OpenAI quotes come from those partners rather than from OpenAI itself. DV Rockerbox says WeightWatchers paid 15.3% less per acquisition on ChatGPT Ads than its blended paid search benchmark, and Triple Whale says 93% of Portland Leather's visitors from ChatGPT Ads were new.

Placement guardrails assess whether a conversation is appropriate for advertising, and Negative Phrases are now available to qualifying advertisers that need exclusions specific to their own policies.

DoubleVerify said on October 5, 2026 that advertisers can now measure ChatGPT Ads as one touchpoint among their other channels inside DV Rockerbox, the attribution business it bought in 2025 for $85 million. It is also developing a brand suitability pilot with OpenAI, still a work in progress.

According to DoubleVerify, Weight Watchers added ChatGPT Ads as a new source of member acquisition, and its attributed cost per acquisition landed 15.3% below its established benchmark during the measured period. OpenAI's same-day post describes the comparison as a blended paid-search benchmark.
“As new advertising channels emerge, we need to understand how they contribute to the broader customer journey,” said Jake Dmochowski, vice president of growth at Weight Watchers.

The release offers no spend, flight dates, acquisition counts, attribution window or benchmark definition, and does not say whether multi-touch attribution or incrementality testing applies to ChatGPT Ads.
The pilot would have independent partners assess OpenAI's suitability policies and guardrails without accessing private user conversations; OpenAI names Integral Ad Science in a parallel pilot.

When former MullenLowe U.S. CEO Frank Cartagena launched his own creative shop, OK Future, he wanted to test how much generative AI would let his agency of four people punch above its weight.

Its first work, Goodwipes’ “Meet Asstra,” a spoof of OpenAI’s commercial for its AI model Astra, went from concept to execution in four days with generative AI tools and curbed the projected $700,000 production costs. A minute-long produced commercial typically takes about six weeks, he said.

Goodwipes and OK Future handled the script, character building, storyboarding and edits; tools including ArtCraft, Seedance and OpenAI’s Astra visualized and voiced the characters and produced the location.

The team worked in shifts around the clock on little sleep. “I really wouldn’t recommend that this be the norm of a project. It’s just an unsustainable pace,” Cartagena said. “It’s a total pressure cooker.”
The spot drove more than 750,000 Reddit views in its first 48 hours and has since reached almost 1.5 million views across subreddits, with more than 800 shares, according to a company spokesperson.
Advancements in AI are helping Walmart save money, which it is, in turn, reinvesting in customer experience improvements, according to U.S. CEO David Guggina.

“We have been leaning into AI for quite some time — we've had physical AI in our supply chain for over seven years — and you can see it reshaping our company, reshaping our customer value proposition,” Guggina said in a conversation with Goldman Sachs’ Katharine McShane.

The gains show most in e-commerce: sales grew 24% year over year in Q2, the 10th consecutive quarter of more than 20% growth. Guggina credited AI-driven efficiencies — faster delivery and cost savings — that were reinvested into competitive pricing and customer experience.

Sparky, which Guggina describes as “becoming more and more capable,” is central to those improvements. Weekly engagement with Sparky has grown 60% quarter over quarter, and its new visual search has led to a 57% spike in conversion compared with text-based searches.

Guggina is also “really happy” with partnerships with external AI agents like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini, which most often deep link customers to Walmart with “fantastic conversion rates.” That contrasts with Amazon, which last month moved to block Meta’s new AI assistant Muse from its site. Many customers arriving via ChatGPT and Gemini are new or returning, with a “very high” organic repeat rate.

blocks.cap: One empty chair, one self-typing machine: the 1 in 6 Meta ad launches run by AI at Ads Uploader

blocks.x: Ads Uploader, a bulk ad-submission platform for Meta, published September 2026 figures showing that AI agents connected directly to the service accounted for 17.5% of the 36,289 batches submitted through it, according to the company.

Applied to the total, that share works out to about 6,350 agent batches over the month, or roughly 212 a day on a 30-day window. The same release puts the month's output at 286,137 Meta ads, about 9,500 a day.

A batch counts as agent-made when an AI agent submits it through the platform's MCP server or its command-line interface. The definition is based on the channel, not on the degree of autonomy, and the release does not split supervised from unsupervised batches.
"A lot of advertisers already have an agent doing the setup work," said Chris Pollard, founder of Ads Uploader. "Last month about 1 in 6 batch launches on our platform came from one."
The data is supplied by the vendor, covers a single month and a single ad platform, and has not been audited. The figures arrive as Meta, Amazon and X open their own ad systems to agents.

OpenAI has launched a virtual try-on feature for ChatGPT users. When users browse clothing and accessories on ChatGPT, they can click the “try on” button, take or upload an image of themselves and then generate images of themselves wearing those products.
Shoppers can save products to Favorites or make a folder in their ChatGPT Library. The features are available on ChatGPT's website and mobile app.

As OpenAI adds shopping features, more retailers are experimenting with the platform: David's Bridal set up shop on Shopify's Agentic Storefronts for ChatGPT in April, and Etsy debuted its ChatGPT app in May.

With try-on, OpenAI is catching up to Google, which debuted virtual try-on for women's tops in 2023, then extended it to dresses and shoes. A 2024 Perfect Corp. survey found brands using virtual try-on saw sales conversion rates more than double.
Google Ads now lets you preview the assets generated by Google AI for your Google Ads AI Max campaigns, in a new “Text customization asset previews” section of the Search campaigns help page.

“Use asset previews to view sample text assets generated by Google AI for your campaign… to see whether generated text assets conform to your defined brand and text guidelines before you opt in to text customization or launch a new campaign.”

Asset examples are mostly generated in under 30 seconds and are available in all languages supported by text customization, including English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, German, Japanese, and Dutch.
When you provide a final landing page URL, Google AI automatically generates up to 10 example headlines and descriptions. You don't need to opt in to text customization to view them.

Pinterest has introduced Beauty Guides, a new AI-based feature. It turns hair and nail Pins into personalized, actionable guides, helping people actually recreate the styles they discover on Pinterest.

Pinterest's visual recognition technology analyzes the hairstyle, color, nail shape, finish and other details in a Pin, and a large language model (LLM) organizes them into what to ask for at the salon, the process, similar styles, related products and step-by-step instructions. Users open a hair or nail Pin in close-up and tap 'Get the Guide.'

Matt Madrigal, chief product and technology officer (CPTO), said, "People come to Pinterest with a clear point of view, even when they can't put the style they want into words." The feature is one example of 'Pinterest Intelligence,' which combines first-party data, visual recognition and purpose-built AI models.

More than 85% of Pinterest users said they discover new beauty trends on Pinterest before anywhere else. Beauty Guides is rolling out first to iOS users in the U.S., with plans to expand to more regions and product categories.

Most of eHealth's customers call during Medicare's roughly 54-day open enrollment window, about half a million calls, and 70% to 80% buy by phone, which left some waiting six hours for a licensed agent.

The health insurance agency now uses Regal's LLM-based voice agent, Alice, to prescreen callers. According to data Regal provided to CX Dive, Alice answers every call immediately, earns 77% "exceptional" satisfaction ratings and has a 27% higher purchase rate than eHealth had with human screeners from an outsourced call center.

The deployment began in February 2025 as an after-hours pilot. Because regulations require an uninterrupted privacy statement, Regal built a "static node" the agent reads without being interrupted before handing callers back to a human agent.
Compliance was a key stakeholder from the start. "For any business that's regulated it's not a plug-and-play solution," said Atul Kumar, eHealth's VP of product and AI.

Meta announced a range of ad updates at its Advertising Week presentation in New York, including an improved business assistant, an expansion of its creative tools for brands and new shopping experiences.

Meta is beefing up its AI-powered business assistant, which provides conversational guidance on key ad creation elements, by adding new creative insights and giving it more memory and context: “the context of what you tried last quarter, your seasonality, and the goals you’ve described,” Meta said.

Meta is also testing importing tools that let brands upload their strategy and brand voice guidelines, adding agentic capacity so the assistant can generate creative, update targeting and change an ad's budget via conversational prompts, and testing scheduled tasks such as recurring performance reports and alerts.
Ads Creative Studio is expanding to more advertisers, the Meta Ads MCP server now supports more use cases for third-party AI tools, and Customer Lifecycle Strategy is available to all advertisers.

In Advantage+ creative, generating video from existing static assets is now generally available; Ads Creative Studio adds tools to change hooks, adjust audio and clip length, add text overlays and captions, or change end scenes.
Meta is working with Shopify on direct checkout via Meta Business Agent on Messenger, and testing similar checkout options for Meta AI with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify and Stripe.
